translations.answer: AMASS v1 unifies 15 marker-based mocap datasets in a common human SMPL-H representation. It does not check target-robot joints, contacts, collisions, torque limits, or closed-loop trackability. In an engineering pipeline, AMASS should remain the human-source layer; only robot-specific retargeting and dynamic closed-loop filtering should produce training labels.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The source sequences are licensed AMASS/SMPL-H records with explicit model versions.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Robot retargeting and closed-loop feasibility filtering are implemented as separate downstream stages.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Humanoid platforms receiving motions retargeted from human data
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Any simulator used for downstream closed-loop feasibility checks
translations.confidence_rationale: The full paper and pinned official tools clearly define AMASS as a unified human surface-motion representation, while the public code exposes human-data preparation rather than robot constraints. Confidence is capped because the effect of each downstream retargeting/filtering design is robot-specific.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines the marker-to-SMPL-H reconstruction scope and validates human surface reconstruction, not robot tracking feasibility.
